newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end flat, new PM appointment ignored.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end flat, new PM appointment ignored.

text.p: Stocks closed nearly flat on Tuesday after a day of narrow fluctuations with investors awaiting a cabinet reshuffle due on Wednesday, brokers said.

"The market showed little interest in the new prime minister. But tomorrow it will react, either positively or negatively, when a new finance minister is named," said Yoo Jae-kyong of Daishin Securities.
President Kim Young-sam appointed Koh Kun, 59, a former mayor of Seoul, as the new prime minister in the morning.
The composite stock index ended 0.33 of a point higher at 679.97.
Volume totalled 28.06 million shares, compared with 26.96 million on Monday. Gainers outpaced losers 443 to 351.

Brokers said falling customer deposits with securities houses were weighing on the market. The deposits were estimated at 2.86 trillion won on Monday, compared with this year's high of 3.05 trillion won on February 15.

Investors were also disappointed as the government showed no signs of raising the foreign stock ownership limit, contrary to expectations. The ceiling is scheduled to be raised to 23 percent this year from 20 percent, but no time has been set.
Brokers said foreign buying weakened because of the sagging value of the won against the dollar.
The won depreciated about 2.25 percent against the dollar from the beginning of this year due to the dollar's strength against the yen and the widening trade deficit.
Brokers said margin loan calls in March would erode market sentiment for the time being.
About 750 billion won worth of such loans must be repaid this month, they said.
